brief_summary: Five-row by three-column matrix comparing ANSI, ISO, and JIS physical keyboard layouts across Enter key shape, Left Shift width, spacebar width, extra key count, and total key count on a full-size board. ANSI renders as a plain baseline column; ISO and JIS cells are outlined in amber wherever they diverge from ANSI.
data_sources: ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'ANSI uses a wide horizontal rectangle, one row tall. ISO and JIS both use a tall, L-shaped Enter that spans two rows'
ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'ISO and JIS shrink the Left Shift key from ANSI's 2.25u down to 1.25u'

ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'JIS shrinks the spacebar from the standard 6.25u down to roughly 4u and fills the freed width with three extra thumb-row keys'
ansi-iso-jis-keyboard-layout-guide.mdx § 'The three layouts, physically' — 'A full-size ANSI board runs 104 keys; ISO runs 105; JIS runs 109' citing switchandclick.com/ansi-vs-iso-layout/
